newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHKELE SAYS ZILE HAS TOUGH TASK IN NEW GOVERNMENT.
newsitem.headline: SHKELE SAYS ZILE HAS TOUGH TASK IN NEW GOVERNMENT.

text.p: Outgoing Prime Minister Andris Shkele said Finance Minster Robert Zile, to be included in the new government, was determined to aim for a balanced budget but faced a tough task to withstand political pressure.
"The finance minister will maintain a balanced budget but I understand what political pressure might be directed towards him," Shkele told a news conference.
He warned that unleashing inflation by increasing salaries and pensions from borrowed funds ahead of elections might ruin the reforms which have started bearing their first fruit.
"The amount of cash in circulation has grown 14.5 times at the current inflation rate of 7.5 percent, a lot of it going into consumption," Shkele said.
Shkele said any deviation from the tough reform line would only result in worsening of the social conditions, hitting especially hard those worst off.
He said the government as a team has to be made responsible for fulfilling the budget instead of leaving only the prime minister and the finance minister in charge.
Shkele also said that the country's favourable credit rating, awarded earlier this year, was also a result of hard hitting but necessary reforms.
He said continued fiscal austerity would have enabled increased pensions next year in addition to the current twice-yearly indexation against inflation.
He also said that Guntar Krasts, picked to replace Shkele as premier, did not believe that a budget deficit was unavoidable.
The Democratic Party Saimnieks, the biggest party in the seven-party ruling coalition has already made attempts to introduce changes in the new pension law.
This caused rows with Welfare Minster Vladimir Makarov who said the proposed amendments lacked the funds to back them.
